expected_invariant: Planar and prism meshes are intrinsically flat, so traces must equal straight lines of the development; Steiner distances with nested point sets are nonincreasing in k and bounded below by chords.
experiment: Trace declared geodesics; compare with exact developments; re-derive lengths by a second ciw implementation (strip layout from edge lengths); compare Dijkstra with a dense Floyd-Warshall and, when installed, scipy.sparse.csgraph; sandwich traced lengths by Steiner distances.
failure_modes_checked: vertex hits (refused, none occurred in the declared set)
tracing through a face without an exit edge
graph duplicates from shared face edges
scipy absent (Floyd-Warshall only; the Dijkstra finding is then numerically_verified)

basis.derivation: With k = 2^j - 1 the node sets are nested and every face keeps all node pairs, so each coarser graph edge is an edge of the finer graph; every graph path is a surface path, which is at least as long as the chord

findings.claim: Nested Steiner-graph distances never increase with k and never fall below the chord

uncertainty.basis: double-precision rounding of deterministic geometry (observed 1e-15 relative)

basis.notes: No scanned surface, device or calibration was acquired; the computation is synthetic.

findings.claim: Straightest geodesics on a mesh reconstructed from a real scan reproduce the geodesics of the scanned physical surface

hypothesis: Unfolding across edges (straight in faces, equal angles at edges) yields exact straightest geodesics on developable meshes, and graph distances bound polyhedral distances from above.
input_data: six declared sphere geodesics (chart point, heading)
mathematical_model: Straightest geodesic: in each face a straight segment; at an edge the direction keeps its edge component and the magnitude of its perpendicular component (rotation about the edge). Distances: Dijkstra on the edge graph and on the graph of k Steiner points per edge (all pairs inside each face); vertex hits are refused.
numerical_result: Plane traces exact to 8.9e-16; prism-cylinder traces match the development to 8.0e-15; unfolded strip length equals traced length to 3.1e-15 over 42 sphere traces (statuses ['completed']); edge Dijkstra agrees with its reference shortest-path implementations to 8.9e-16; Steiner distances to traced endpoints exceed the traced length by mean 3.01e-02 (k=1), 1.29e-02 (k=3), 5.30e-03 (k=7).
observation_model: No physical observation; traced endpoints, lengths and graph distances in normalized units.

physical_validation_status.statement: Physical validation requires acquired hardware evidence; none was acquired for this task.

recommended_next_task: T039: measure convergence of these traces and distances under refinement; then implement an exact polyhedral distance (MMP or ICH) as an independent reference.

title: Build a triangle-mesh intrinsic geodesic solver.
uncertainty: Deterministic computation; floating-point rounding only (differences at 1e-15 relative). The strip layout and Floyd-Warshall are ciw code (same origin); only the scipy comparison is independent. The Steiner sandwich is consistent with, but does not prove, that the traced geodesics are shortest paths.
unresolved_assumptions: Vertex hits are refused rather than continued by the Polthier-Schmies angle-bisection rule.
The Steiner graph is an approximation scheme; no exact polyhedral (MMP/ICH) distance is implemented.
Traced geodesics are shortest paths only when no shorter corridor exists; not proved here.
